title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies that create or deploy artificial intelligence systems to produce detailed reports describing their capabilities, potential risks, and societal impact. This law aims to increase transparency and help regulators monitor and ensure the responsible use of AI in China.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a set of rules aimed at regulating the development and deployment of artificial intelligence in the United States. It focuses on ensuring AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values while encouraging innovation.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act is a U.S. law designed to bolster the country’s AI workforce by promoting education, training, and research initiatives. It establishes funding and collaborative programs to attract, develop, and retain top AI talent, ensuring the United States remains competitive in technology innovation.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This bill requires developers of artificial intelligence systems to provide detailed functional bills of materials that list all components, data sources, and dependencies used in the AI, improving transparency and traceability. It also includes additional provisions related to the regulation, safety, and other related aspects of AI deployment.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act is designed to guide schools, teachers, and students in responsibly adopting AI tools, ensuring transparency, fairness, and privacy protections. It establishes educational standards and professional development requirements to help educators effectively and ethically integrate AI into classroom instruction.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law designed to improve students’ understanding of artificial intelligence in public schools. It calls for AI‑focused curriculum standards and teacher training to ensure that schools are prepared for the growing role of AI in education.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: This act establishes safety standards for AI‑powered toys designed for children, ensuring they are physically safe, non‑harmful, and protect children’s privacy. It requires manufacturers to test, certify compliance, and adhere to data‑handling and content‑moderation guidelines before the toys can be sold.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives asserts that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to full transparency about these projects. It also stresses that such communities deserve local autonomy to decide how these data centers affect them.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would prohibit the establishment of AI data centers on federal property, preventing large‑scale AI infrastructure from being built on public lands. This aims to protect federal lands from the environmental, energy, and privacy concerns associated with such high‑density facilities.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 seeks to ensure that AI technologies used in veterans’ services are developed and deployed responsibly, with clear standards for safety, transparency, and privacy. It creates oversight mechanisms and a dedicated body to monitor AI applications, address ethical concerns, and protect veterans from potential harms.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: This Act aims to protect people and businesses from being misled or exploited by false claims created by artificial intelligence. It sets rules for developers and users to verify authenticity, report misuse, and imposes penalties for producing or spreading fabricated exploitation.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 requires the government to study how artificial intelligence is used in the judicial system and to set up a dedicated oversight body to monitor and evaluate those uses. The act also establishes guidelines for transparency, accountability, and regular audits to ensure that any AI tools employed in court are fair, explainable, and do not compromise the integrity of judicial proceedings.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The bill requires the government to produce a report on how artificial intelligence is used when accessing unminimized information collected under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA). It also addresses additional related issues and provides guidance for future AI-related intelligence activities.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to stop companies from using software that conspires to fix prices or limit competition. It establishes rules and penalties to ensure algorithms act fairly and transparently in markets.

title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This act aims to reduce the United States’ reliance on Chinese artificial‑intelligence technology and supply chains, strengthening national security and economic independence. It proposes measures to limit imports of Chinese AI products, boost domestic development, and enforce stricter controls on technology transfers involving China.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act is designed to broaden the use and representation of AI-generated voices in public and commercial settings. It seeks to establish guidelines that promote transparency, accountability, and fairness in how these AI voices are created and deployed.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a proposed federal law designed to regulate artificial intelligence technologies, focusing on safety, accountability, and transparency in their use. It establishes guidelines and oversight mechanisms for the development, deployment, and monitoring of AI systems across multiple industries.

title: LEARN AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
summary: The LEARN AI Act is a proposed law aimed at regulating the development and use of artificial intelligence. It seeks to promote transparency, accountability, and safety in AI systems to protect users and ensure ethical practices.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a law that protects the personal information of children when it is collected, used, or shared by AI technologies. It sets strict rules and safeguards to ensure that minors' data is handled securely, transparently, and with their best interests in mind.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 requires schools to teach students about artificial intelligence so they can use it safely and responsibly. It sets up guidelines and training for teachers, provides resources for schools, and establishes a federal oversight body to monitor progress.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 33 - 0.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2025 seeks to expand AI education across K‑12, college, and workforce programs by providing new funding, resources, and partnerships. It aims to equip students, teachers, and professionals with AI skills through curriculum development, training initiatives, and collaborative research with industry.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a U.S. law designed to protect artificial‑intelligence developers by making it illegal to steal or illegally copy AI models. It imposes penalties, including fines and potential imprisonment, on anyone who unlawfully obtains, reproduces, or distributes a protected AI model.
